memory: I've been on a variety of medications over the years to manage my health conditions. It's important for me to keep track of everything, including dosages and any changes to my medication regimen. Regular reviews with my doctor help ensure that I'm on the right medications and that any necessary adjustments can be made.I've been taking metformin 1000 mg twice daily for several years to manage my Type 2 Diabetes. It helps keep my blood sugar in check, but my A1C still hovers around 6.9%. My doctor recently suggested adding a GLP-1 receptor agonist, semaglutide(Ozempic), at a low dose. So far, I've noticed that it helps control my appetite, which is a nice bonus. I also check my fasting blood sugar at home regularly, and it usually stays between 125-130 mg/dL.I take losartan 50 mg once daily to manage my high blood pressure. It's been keeping my readings mostly in the 135-140/80-90 mmHg range, which is a bit higher than ideal. My doctor suggests that stress management and reducing sodium intake can help instead of increasing the dosage. I also take a daily magnesium supplement, which I've heard can help with blood pressure regulation.I take levothyroxine 75 mcg every morning to manage my hypothyroidism. I make sure to take it on an empty stomach and wait at least 30 minutes before eating. My last TSH test came back at 2.1 mIU/L, which is within the normal range, so my doctor hasn't changed my dosage in years. I do notice if I miss a dose, I feel sluggish the next day, so I keep a pill organizer to stay on track.I take acetaminophen as needed for mild pain to manage my osteoarthritis. When my joints are really acting up, my doctor prescribed meloxicam 7.5 mg, an anti-inflammatory. I don't take it every day because I don't want to overdo it on NSAIDs, but it definitely helps when my knees and hands are particularly stiff. My doctor also suggested trying glucosamine supplements, but I can't say for sure if they've made a difference.I recently adjusted my vitamin D intake after my blood test showed low levels at 22 ng/mL(normal is above 30 ng/mL). Now I take vitamin D3 2,000 IU daily. I also take calcium supplements since my last bone density scan showed early signs of osteopenia. My doctor recommended combining it with vitamin K2 to help with absorption.I take atorvastatin 10 mg daily to help manage my cholesterol. My LDL was a bit high at 130 mg/dL, and my triglycerides were at 140 mg/dL, so my doctor thought a low-dose statin would be beneficial. So far, my cholesterol numbers have been improving, and I haven't experienced any side effects, which is a relief since some people report muscle aches with statins.I take a daily multivitamin, omega-3 supplements for heart health, and probiotics to help with digestion. Since my gallbladder was removed a few years ago, I sometimes take digestive enzymes if I eat something heavier. Losing my gallbladder changed the way I digest fatty foods, so I have to be mindful of that.I keep an eye on potential medication interactions, especially since I take both losartan and meloxicam occasionally. My doctor warned me that NSAIDs can sometimes affect kidney function, so I try not to take meloxicam too often. I also make sure to take my thyroid medication separately from my calcium and iron supplements, as they can interfere with absorption.I believe my medication routine is working well for me. It's a lot to keep track of, but I stay organized with a pill planner and use reminders on my phone. I also focus on lifestyle changes to avoid relying on medications alone. My goal is to stay as healthy as possible and avoid unnecessary prescriptions by managing things naturally when I can!
